form.title: Uganda national Adverse Drug Reaction / Adverse Event Following Immunisation reporting form ("NDA ADR reporting form"; MoH MTC guideline Annex 3.2 title: "Adverse Reaction Report/Adverse Event Following Immunization Form")
form.version: unknown: no version number, form code or print date found. Field list taken from the form reproduced in the Uganda National Training Manual for Health Workers on Pharmacovigilance, Trainee Handbook (MoH/NDA, file signed 13 Feb 2020) [S1]. An older ADR-only MoH/NDA form (c. 2015) [S2] marked six fields mandatory; those marks are carried here as the best available evidence for required fields.

fields.field: Report is about: drug / vaccine / other (medical device, equipment, blood products, antivenom), with specify
fields.medsyncSource: derived: 'drug' for pharmacy-raised reports; vaccine reports are out of scope (AEFI route)

fields.field: Event type: suspected ADR / AEFI / suspected or observed inefficacy / observed poor-quality product / medication error / suspected counterfeit
fields.medsyncSource: ask (reporter picks; MedSync pre-selects from the screen the report was raised on)

fields.phiNote: initials only leave MedSync; the NDA manual asks for full name for follow-up and de-duplication [S1]: legal answer needed

fields.medsyncSource: derived from date of birth in patient record and reaction onset date
fields.phiNote: age only, never date of birth
district only; low re-identification risk but confirm
do not include; NDA follow-up goes through the reporter: legal answer needed

fields.medsyncSource: derived from LMP or antenatal record, else ask
first administration (ward MAR) or first dispense date
ward administration record where held, else ask
prescription (copied as written; MedSync never converts doses)

fields.field: Vaccine dose number; diluent name, batch and expiry; time of reconstitution (vaccines only)
fields.medsyncSource: not applicable: AEFI handled by the immunisation route
ask (reporter); MedSync suggests from outcome and admission data but does not decide

fields.field: Reason for seriousness: death / prolonged hospitalisation / persistent disability / congenital anomaly / life threatening / other important medical condition (specify)
All drugs in the last 3 months incl. self-medication and herbal: generic and brand name, batch and expiry, dates started and stopped, dose, route, frequency, indication
fields.medsyncSource: active and recent prescriptions and dispensing (90 days); medication history from clerking/reconciliation; herbal and OTC: ask

fields.field: Description of reaction as observed, and any treatment given
fields.medsyncSource: ask (reporter narrative); treatment given can be listed from prescriptions after onset
fields.phiNote: free text: MedSync warns the reporter not to type names, phone numbers or hospital numbers

fields.medsyncSource: ask; defaults to the date the suspected reaction was recorded

fields.field: Date patient notified the health system of the event
fields.medsyncSource: date the suspected reaction was first recorded in MedSync
lab results (reporter selects which to include)
fields.phiNote: values and dates only, no lab accession numbers

fields.field: Additional relevant information (medical history, allergies, failure of efficacy)
fields.medsyncSource: problem list, allergy list, clerking history

fields.field: Outcome: recovering / recovered / recovered with sequelae / continuing / not recovered / died / unknown
fields.medsyncSource: ask; prompts a follow-up update at discharge or death

fields.phiNote: reporter identity is disclosed by the reporter's choice; form states identities kept strictly confidential [S3]
reporter's own work contacts; one of the two is needed for a valid report [S1]

fields.medsyncSource: set when the report is marked sent

routes.route: Online e-reporting form (WHO-UMC primary reporting, feeds the national VigiFlow database)
routes.notes: Listed by NDA as its online reporting address in the 2015/16 annual PV report [S5]. Entry page was live on 2026-10-24 (asks email, language, reporter type, captcha) [S6]; current NDA endorsement not confirmed because NDA pages could not be opened.

routes.route: Med Safety mobile app (Android and iOS)
routes.notes: Launched by NDA on 27 Feb 2020 for the public and health workers [S8]; sends reports directly to the National Pharmacovigilance Centre [S7]. Not designed for COVID-19 vaccine AEFI [S7].
Collected by PV focal persons and drug regulatory officers [S7] or by Regional Pharmacovigilance Centre coordinators at regional referral hospitals (13 in 2015/16) [S5], or sent to NPC offices [S1].
Address printed in the training manual [S1] and older form [S2]. 53% of reports came by email in the year before Feb 2020 [S8].
0791415555 per training manual [S1]; MTC guideline 2025 lists WhatsApp without the number [S9].

routes.route: NDA Market Complaint Form (product quality, suspected substandard or falsified)
routes.notes: Named on the NDA home page ('Market Complaint Request Form - Part 1') [S10] and in the MTC guideline as Annex 3.3, report to NDA and the supplier [S9]; the national ADR form also carries 'poor-quality product' and 'suspected counterfeit' event types [S1]. Form itself not opened.
Same combined form carries AEFI [S1][S9]; vaccine events go through the immunisation programme route and are out of scope for the pharmacy module.

causality.definition: Event or laboratory abnormality with a plausible time relationship to drug intake; cannot be explained by disease or other drugs; response to withdrawal plausible (pharmacologically, pathologically); event definitive pharmacologically or phenomenologically; rechallenge satisfactory, if necessary. [S12, paraphrase close to source; copy verbatim from source before signature]

Event or laboratory abnormality with a reasonable time relationship to drug intake; unlikely to be attributed to disease or other drugs; response to withdrawal clinically reasonable; rechallenge not required. [S12]
Event or laboratory abnormality with a reasonable time relationship to drug intake; could also be explained by disease or other drugs; information on drug withdrawal may be lacking or unclear. [S12]
Event or laboratory abnormality with a time to drug intake that makes a relationship improbable (but not impossible); disease or other drugs provide plausible explanations. [S12]
Event or laboratory abnormality; more data for proper assessment needed, or additional data under examination. [S12]
Report suggesting an adverse reaction; cannot be judged because information is insufficient or contradictory; data cannot be supplemented or verified. [S12]

seriousness: Requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation [S13]
Results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity [S13]

Other medically important event or condition: medical and scientific judgement; such events should also usually be considered serious [S13]; Uganda form wording: 'Other important medical condition (specify)' [S1]
gaps: NDA 'Guidelines on detecting and reporting adverse drug reactions in Uganda' (https://www.nda.or.ug/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/GUIDELINES-detecting-and-reporting-ADR.pdf) could not be opened (three attempts, site error); title known from search only, year unknown.
No current NDA form version, form code or print date found; field list is from the 2020 training manual reproduction, required marks from a c. 2015 form.
NDA product safety pages, the 'NDA Adverse Drug Reporting System' link and the Market Complaint Form could not be opened; current online URL not confirmed by NDA itself.
Reporting timelines conflict: 24 to 48 hours serious / 15 calendar days non-serious [S1] versus 48 hours serious / 7 days non-serious [S9]; the regulations set no timeline [S3][S4].
No NDA statement found on accepting ICH E2B(R3) XML or any API submission from a facility system; VigiFlow accepts E2B from compliant systems [S15] but access is via the national centre.
Med Safety app store links and the reporter-type options on the e-reporting form were not captured.

Patient identifiers: NDA asks for full name, village and telephone [S1]; MedSync policy is initials only. Needs a legal answer under Ugandan data protection law (Data Protection and Privacy Act 2019 not opened).
Medication-error reporting: carried as an event type on the ADR form [S1][S9]; the PV regulations do not address medication errors [S3][S4].
